subject: EdgeCraft evaluation — unified econ comparison & next tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@edgecraft.ai>, Alice Monroe <alice@edgecraft.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeCraft evaluation — economics + next tests

Hi Tom / Alice — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Short recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Call TL;DR (what you told us)
- Primary goal: reduce per-inference unit cost for interactive assistants (high 95th percentile latency targets) while keeping model quality at-or-better than your current hosted endpoint.
- Current vendor (BigCloud) quoted ~ $35 / 1M tokens for the base gpt-like endpoint in their standard tier; they also pointed to different pricing if you reserve capacity.
- Key constraints: SSO + VPC, audit logs, and strict data retention settings for logs (30 days).

What Redwood proposes for the evaluation (high level)
1) Comparative unit-econ test: run 1M-token baseline to compare effective cost/tokens across three configurations — BigCloud-managed endpoint (your existing), Redwood Hosted (standard), Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) — using the same tokenized corpus. We'll measure per-1M effective cost, mean/95th latency, and throughput with the same request mix.
2) Microbench scenarios: batch-size sweep (1, 8, 32), cache warm-vs-cold (KV cache hit rates: 10%, 50%, 90%), and quantization variants (FP16 vs 4-bit).
3) Real-world simulation: 100k interactive sessions sampled from your corpus to measure tail latency and model-behavior regressions.

Key assumptions in our unit-econ worksheet (attached: unit-econ-assumptions.xlsx)
- Tokenization parity: we'll use the same tokenizer and exact input set you provide.
- Network egress: excluded from per-1M token numbers (we'll call out separately).
- Cache warm-up: measured explicitly; final reported per-token cost will show both cold and warm amortized numbers.

Initial numbers (directional, from our benchmarks):
- Redwood Hosted (standard batching + prefix cache): ~$12–14 / 1M tokens (warm cache, batch=8)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved, aggressive batching + 90% cache hit): ~$6–8 / 1M tokens (depends on committed throughput and model quantization)
- These are illustrative; finals depend on your workload mix.

Action items / asks:
1) Please share a 20k–50k token sample corpus (S3 link preferred) and an anonymized session distribution.
2) Confirm whether procurement prefers an NDA-first path or if we can proceed under the standard eval T&Cs.
3) If possible, grant a read-only IAM role or temporary S3 share for the dataset so our test harness can be wired.

Attachments: edgecraft-mutual-action-plan.pdf (draft MAP), unit-econ-assumptions.xlsx

Proposed timeline
- This week: dataset + access + sign MAP (if useful)
- Next 7–10 days: run 1M token baseline + microbench sweep
- Follow-up: readout call with economics + recommendations

I copied Ben and Marissa to coordinate engineering and benchmarks. Ben — can you confirm the test harness details below (sample rates, tokenization script)?

Thanks — looking forward to the data and running a clean apples-to-apples comparison.

— Karthik

1) We'll share a 30k-token anonymized corpus via S3 by EOD tomorrow (Alice is on this).
2) Procurement prefers NDA-first for anything that includes internal logs; I copied them. If you can share a redlined NDA by tomorrow we can fast-track.
3) For the BigCloud baseline, I'll provision a time-limited API key for your test harness and include an account owner contact so you can run the exact same workload. Expect the key and details with the dataset.

A couple of asks from our side: 
- Please call out any non-obvious differences in token accounting across vendors (e.g., system prompts, tool-calls).
- Can you run a latency breakdown that separates model time vs network vs batching overhead? That helps our infra folks.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeCraft evaluation — economics + next tests

Karthik — quick internal note before we send the test spec to them. Recommended test matrix (details for harness):

1) Token sample normalization: run tokenization on the provided corpus with the same tokenizer used in production (script: tokenize.py). Produce a token histogram to validate parity.
2) 1M-token baseline: sequentially feed requests to reproduce current user mix. Measure: total tokens, avg tokens/request, compute time, GPU time, queue wait, network RTT.
3) Batch sweep: batch sizes [1,8,16,32] with concurrency adjusted to keep p95 latency < target buckets (we'll record p50/p95/p99).
4) Cache scenarios: cold (0% hit), medium (40–60%), and warm (80–95%). We'll simulate prefix reuse by replaying sessions.
5) Quantization: FP16 vs 4-bit with perf regressions and quality checks (we'll run a small eval set for perplexity / instruction-following checks).

Tooling:
- We will use the Redwood test harness (attached instructions) and will require the BigCloud time-limited API key and an S3 endpoint to store raw logs.

Estimated runtime: full matrix ~ 48 hours if we run in parallel on dedicated instances; can compress to 24 hours with burst capacity.

I'll prepare the canonical test-run JSON and pass to Tom/Alice after they confirm data+keys. Also recommend we instrument a short prompt-level scoring set to detect hallucination/regressions (10k tokens).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
